questions.text: What does "must" express in modal deduction?
questions.correct: Near-certainty based on evidence
questions.hint: "Must expresses near-certainty: the available evidence almost forces the conclusion." ✅

questions.text: Why is "the data must be the case" more careful than "the data shows"?
opts: It acknowledges the gap between evidence and conclusion
questions.correct: It acknowledges the gap between evidence and conclusion
questions.hint: "Epistemically more careful because it acknowledges the gap between evidence and conclusion." ✅

questions.text: What does "should have called" imply about whether she called?
opts: She didn't call — and this was a mistake
questions.correct: She didn't call — and this was a mistake
questions.hint: "By implication, not calling was a mistake." — should have = she didn't, and should have. ✅

questions.text: What is the difference between "needn't have done" and "shouldn't have done"?
opts: "Needn't" = done but unnecessary; "shouldn't" = done and was a mistake
questions.correct: "Needn't" = done but unnecessary; "shouldn't" = done and was a mistake
questions.hint: "Needn't have done" = unnecessary. "Shouldn't have done" = a mistake. Different meanings. ✅

questions.text: Daniyar says the authorities "must have known" by the 1970s. What does this mean?
opts: He is almost certain they knew — evidence existed
questions.correct: He is almost certain they knew — evidence existed
questions.hint: "Must have known" = past deduction, near-certainty. Evidence: official reports described the shrinkage. ✅

questions.text: Dr. Yerlan's key question is:
opts: Were modern standards applied to past decision-makers, or genuine standards being ignored at the time?
Should the sea have been saved?
How much did the disaster cost?
questions.correct: Were modern standards applied to past decision-makers, or genuine standards being ignored at the time?
questions.hint: "Are you applying modern standards to past decision-makers, or genuine standards that existed and were ignored at the time?" ✅

questions.text: In Listening 1, what does Kamila argue about the WKU logo on the bag?
opts: The other team definitely took it
It makes confusion almost impossible — can't have been confused
questions.correct: It makes confusion almost impossible — can't have been confused
questions.hint: "That can't be right — our bag has the WKU logo. They couldn't have confused it." ✅

questions.text: What does Kamila say about wasting time speculating?
opts: They needn't have speculated — should have called straight away
questions.correct: They needn't have speculated — should have called straight away
questions.hint: "We needn't have wasted time speculating — we should have called the coach straight away." ✅

questions.text: What does Daniyar say about the fishermen staying near the Aral Sea?
opts: They must have stayed because they had no viable alternative
They didn't know the sea was shrinking
questions.correct: They must have stayed because they had no viable alternative
questions.hint: "They must have stayed because they had no viable alternative — no one gave them one." ✅

questions.text: What does Amir say about "should have known"?
opts: Only valid if knowledge existed and was being ignored at the time
Should always be replaced with "could have known"
questions.correct: Only valid if knowledge existed and was being ignored at the time
questions.hint: "'Should have known' only works if the knowledge was available and was being ignored." ✅

questions.text: Who suggests the caretaker might have moved the kit bag?
questions.correct: Amir
questions.hint: "The caretaker! He's been cleaning all evening. He might have moved it to the storage room." — Amir. ✅

questions.text: What does Zhibek conclude after calling the coach?
opts: It must still be in the building — someone must have moved it
The other team has it after all
questions.correct: It must still be in the building — someone must have moved it
questions.hint: "It must still be in the building somewhere. Someone must have moved it without realising." ✅

questions.text: "She must have left already." — "must have left" expresses:
questions.correct: Past deduction (near-certainty based on evidence)
questions.hint: "must have + pp" = past deduction. Near-certainty from evidence. ✅

questions.text: "He can't have read the report." — "can't have" means:
opts: It's almost certain he didn't read it
questions.correct: It's almost certain he didn't read it
questions.hint: "can't have + pp" = past deduction of impossibility. ✅

questions.text: "She ___ (study) all night — she knows everything."
questions.correct: must have been studying
questions.hint: Evidence → high certainty about ongoing past activity. "She MUST HAVE BEEN STUDYING all night." ✅

questions.text: "You should have told me." — "should have told" means:
opts: You were able to tell me
You didn't tell me — this was wrong/a mistake
questions.correct: You didn't tell me — this was wrong/a mistake
questions.hint: "should have + pp" = criticism/regret. The action (telling) wasn't done, and it should have been. ✅

questions.text: "She needn't have prepared so much." — "needn't have prepared" means:
opts: She prepared but it was unnecessary
questions.correct: She prepared but it was unnecessary
questions.hint: "needn't have + pp" = done but turned out to be unnecessary. ✅

questions.text: Key difference: "could have applied" vs "should have applied":
opts: "Could have" = opportunity existed (observation); "should have" = it was wrong not to (judgement)
questions.correct: "Could have" = opportunity existed (observation); "should have" = it was wrong not to (judgement)
questions.hint: "could have" = observation. "should have" = judgement/criticism. ✅

questions.text: "She should have went." — Error:
questions.correct: "went" should be "gone" — past participle
questions.hint: ✅ "She should have GONE." — must have + PAST PARTICIPLE. "Went" = past simple (wrong). ✅

questions.text: "Was able to finish" vs "could have finished":
opts: "Was able to" = managed it (achievement); "could have" = had ability but didn't use it
questions.correct: "Was able to" = managed it (achievement); "could have" = had ability but didn't use it
questions.hint: "was able to finish" = she finished. "could have finished" = had ability but didn't. ✅

questions.text: "Deduction." In this context:
opts: Reasoning from evidence to a conclusion
questions.correct: Reasoning from evidence to a conclusion
questions.hint: "deduction" = the process of reaching a conclusion from evidence through reasoning.

questions.text: "Retrospective judgement." "Retrospective" means:
questions.correct: Looking back on past events
questions.hint: "retrospective" = relating to or dealing with past events from the perspective of the present.

questions.text: "The evidence warrants must." "Warrants" means:
opts: Justifies or is sufficient reason for
questions.correct: Justifies or is sufficient reason for
questions.hint: "warrant" = to justify; to be sufficient grounds for a conclusion.

questions.text: "She is a perceptive person." "Perceptive" means:
opts: Able to notice and understand things quickly
questions.correct: Able to notice and understand things quickly
questions.hint: "perceptive" = showing insight; quickly noticing and understanding things.

questions.text: "Post-mortem analysis." "Post-mortem" here means:
opts: An analysis done before an event
A review after an event — especially of what went wrong
questions.correct: A review after an event — especially of what went wrong
questions.hint: "post-mortem" (in professional contexts) = a review or analysis that happens after a project or event, to understand what went wrong.
